posts.author: rja4096
posts.content_md:
HI,

Can anyone advise please.

I've got a very simple setup, doing a single beam reflection, using PFG-03m plates 2 and a half inch square, the 3mw Integraf laser and JD-4 developer. Distance from laser to plate is 14 inches.

I'm sure the table is very stable, but think there may be a problem with my developing technique.

When I last used PFG-03m about 2 years ago, I remember exposing and developing for 10 seconds, with good results.

Now when develop with these same timings, the plate goes dark around the edges (about a quarter of an inch thick margin), but does not darken very quickly in the middle.

I've already used 2 of my 6 plates and got really really dim holograms, I'm wondering if this new batch (manuf Jan 06) should need more exposure time - I'm thinking of trying 25 seconds, or does it need longer development.

But this still does not answer why different areas of the plate should develop more quickly.

here is the picture of my setup.

![Image](http://www.holovue.co.uk/reflection.jpg)

Can anyone please help me.

Thanks, Rick

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I know you only have 4 plates left but you may want to try to develop a plate with no exposure. It sounds like the edges of your plates might be fogged.

posts.author: rja4096
posts.content_md:
Thanks Colin,

I guess this would explain whats happening with the edges of the plates. I'm still not sure about how the exposure/developing times appear to need to be longer. 

- I did have another thought, I wonder if the laser diode is on its way out, is this how these things die, or do they suddenly just stop working. - P.S. I have put new batteries in.

Thanks, Rick.

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md: My experience has been that laser diodes die suddenly but not completely. I think they get zapped by static electricity. I have several go that way - and after they go, they still put out light, although it's a much weaker beam, and may have strange uneven patterns.

posts.author: Steve M
posts.content_md:
Rick:

The exposure rating for PFG-03 (2000 microwatts/sec) is 25 times what it is for PFG-01 (80 microwatts/sec) at 633nm. You may be unexposing the hologram.

Your darkening of the edges may be what Colin suggests, fogging on the edges. My first processing of this emulsion caused me to get much greater density on the edges than in the middle also. When Tech Pan came out in the mid 80's, it was also a very fine grain emulsion and a special agitation technique was developed to solve the same problem. I applied a modified technique to 03 and it worked well. Place your plate or film in the tray, emulsion up of course, and agitate with a circular motion for 5 seconds. Let the plate/film rest without agitation for 30 seconds, then repeat the circular motion for 5 seconds. Clockwise or counterclockwise, doesn't matter. Continue to do this for 5 minutes (I always use 5 minutes in a developer to enhance contrast in the image instead of the 2 minutes a lot of people use.) If you're doing a 4x5, then you'll need to use an 8x10 tray to let you create the circular motion using your hand to hold the plate/film. This method gives me complete uniformity in the density across the plate/film. Hope this helps.

Steve
